title: The La Cerra online topo is live
imageAlt: Hand-drawn field notes for the Somewhere sector beside crash pads
teaser: The printed guide has grown into a living online topo with sectors, maps, routes and personal tick lists.
text: The La Cerra online topo is now available. It brings the information from the original guidebook into a format that can grow with the area: sectors can be updated, new routes can be added and corrections no longer have to wait for another printed edition.

parts.text: Every published
sector
combines an overview, approach information, maps, boulder photographs and route details. The central
route directory
makes it possible to search and filter the complete guide instead of moving through the sectors one by one.

Registered climbers can mark routes as climbed, record flashes, add personal grade suggestions and keep their own project list. Community ratings and grade suggestions are shown alongside the route information while individual entries remain attached to the climber's
personal profile

This first public version is a starting point rather than a finished archive. La Cerra still has undeveloped rock, and the online topo will continue to change as reliable information and new material become available. The
topo symbols and visitor information
remain the best place to prepare for a visit.

title: How bouldering at La Cerra began
imageAlt: Pine forest and camper van at La Cerra during the development of the guidebook
teaser: From the first scouting days to a growing community project: the people and stages behind La Cerra.

parts.text: The bouldering potential around La Cerra had been recognised for years. In 2013, the La Sportiva Sardinia Bloc Scouting Team cleaned the first blocks and established a collection of problems that became today's
La Sportiva sector
The development continued through several independent efforts. Eadan Cunningham explored and documented another extensive part of the area, while Florian Schiffer and friends opened
2nd Life
in 2019. Their work showed how much rock was still hidden in the landscape around the agriturismo.

Felix Clotten and Ivanessa Mirastschijski arrived in November 2020, originally planning La Cerra as the final stop of a longer journey. Alberto had already uncovered many blocks on the property, and the visit soon became a project of cleaning loose rock, finding lines and recording the growing number of problems. Sarah and Valle joined the work in
Sushi-Free

A meeting with Martin and Petra from tmms-Verlag turned the idea of a small personal guide into a published topo. Eadan shared his existing information, and Florian Schiffer and the Stuntwerk team contributed the work that became
Stuntblocs
in March 2021. The printed guide published in 2021 brought these separate chapters together and created the foundation for the online topo available today.

text: La Cerra remains an open story. New lines are still possible, but every development depends on careful cleaning, reliable information and respectful behaviour toward the land, its owners and the surrounding nature.
